Let

\[
\vec x=\overrightarrow{AB},\qquad \vec y=\overrightarrow{AC},\qquad \vec z=\overrightarrow{AD},
\]

and choose the orientation so

\[
T=\det(\vec x,\vec y,\vec z)>0.
\]

Then the volume is

\[
V=\frac{T}{6}.
\]

Define the three normal vectors

\[
\vec n_1=\vec y\times \vec z,\qquad
\vec n_2=\vec z\times \vec x,\qquad
\vec n_3=\vec x\times \vec y.
\]

Since the three faces through \(A\) each have area \(1\),

\[
|\vec n_1|=|\vec n_2|=|\vec n_3|=2.
\]

Also

\[
(C-B)\times(D-B)
=(\vec y-\vec x)\times(\vec z-\vec x)
=\vec n_1+\vec n_2+\vec n_3,
\]

so the condition \([BCD]=s\) gives

\[
|\vec n_1+\vec n_2+\vec n_3|=2s.
\]

Now set \(\vec u_i=\vec n_i/2\). Then

\[
|\vec u_1|=|\vec u_2|=|\vec u_3|=1,\qquad
|\vec u_1+\vec u_2+\vec u_3|=s.
\]

Let \(G=(\vec u_i\cdot \vec u_j)\). Write the off-diagonal entries as \(p,q,r\). The condition above gives

\[
s^2=3+2(p+q+r),
\]

so

\[
p+q+r=\frac{s^2-3}{2}.
\]

We need maximize the determinant of \(G\). For fixed diagonal entries and fixed sum \(p+q+r\), \(\det G\) is maximized when

\[
p=q=r=\frac{s^2-3}{6}=:t.
\]

This follows from concavity of \(\log\det\) on positive definite matrices: averaging over all permutations preserves the constraints and cannot decrease the determinant.

Thus

\[
G=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&t&t\\
t&1&t\\
t&t&1
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
t=\frac{s^2-3}{6}.
\]

Its determinant is

\[
\det G=(1-t)^2(1+2t).
\]

Since \(0<s<3\), we have \(-\frac12<t<1\), so this is positive. Now

\[
1-t=\frac{9-s^2}{6},
\qquad
1+2t=\frac{s^2}{3}.
\]

Hence

\[
\sqrt{\det G}
=\frac{s(9-s^2)}{6\sqrt3}.
\]

Finally, if \(N\) is the matrix with columns \(\vec n_1,\vec n_2,\vec n_3\), then

\[
\det N=T^2.
\]

But \(N=2U\), where \(U\) has columns \(\vec u_i\), so

\[
T^2=\det N=8\det U=8\sqrt{\det G}.
\]

Therefore

\[
V^2=\frac{T^2}{36}
=\frac{8}{36}\sqrt{\det G}
=\frac{2}{9}\cdot \frac{s(9-s^2)}{6\sqrt3}.
\]

So

\[
V_{\max}
=\sqrt{\frac{s(9-s^2)}{27\sqrt3}}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\sqrt{\frac{s(9-s^2)}{27\sqrt3}}}
\]
